task: Align the dashboard with the OpenForge design system and land the custom trends range, Quota Policies tab, HA standby badge and contrast rework that came out of the same pass

events.summary: OpenForge portfolio compliance audit (dasomel/openforge docs/gap-issues/nfs-quota-agent-design-system-gap-issue.md) scored the repo 81.8% with two Design System gaps: DESIGN-001 archetype declaration and DESIGN-002 semantic token mapping. Its suggested archetype, Developer Tool, was rejected on review -- a quota-enforcement agent's dashboard is an Operations Dashboard under OpenForge section 6 -- and the corrected archetype is what DESIGN.md declares
events.provenance: dasomel/openforge docs/gap-issues/nfs-quota-agent-design-system-gap-issue.md, generated by the OpenForge Portfolio Compliance Auditor

events.summary: Scoped to DESIGN.md and internal/ui (dashboard.html, server.go, server_test.go). No change to internal/quota, internal/agent, the apply/verify path, CRDs, RBAC or chart privileges. The pre-existing /api/history behaviour of silently returning an empty array when path is omitted was found during verification and deliberately left out -- fixing it breaks the dashboard's stats-only call -- and filed as #96 instead

DESIGN.md declares the Operations Dashboard archetype and maps every color/* token to an OpenForge semantic role with the intentional deviations recorded under ADR-0007 (dffe570). dashboard.html gains a custom trends range whose start/end reach /api/history as RFC3339 and are rejected with 400 when malformed, one-sided or inverted; a Quota Policies tab rendering QuotaPolicy CRs; an HA standby badge driven by a new haActive field on /api/status; and quotaPolicyEnabled on /api/config gated on the same DynamicClient presence handleAPIQuotaPolicies already uses (afb7150)

Contrast defect reproduced by measurement, not by eye: the single border token served as structural boundary, in-container divider and chart/progress track at once, so usage bars and the donut's free arc sat below the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 minimum against surfaceCard, and inkMuted plus the light-theme warning and serious status colors were below 4.5:1 on the 12% tint they actually render over. Every pair was checked with a throwaway contrast script in both themes

Split border into border / borderStrong / track, retuned inkMuted and accent, and let the light-theme status colors diverge from dark so each theme passes on its own. DESIGN.md records the measured pairs and the rule that any palette change is re-measured in both themes before merging

Re-measured every changed pair after the split: normal text at or above 4.5:1, large text and UI boundaries at or above 3:1, status badge text checked against its own 12% color-mix tint over surfaceCard, in light and dark independently. A separate review lane then diffed the DESIGN.md token values literally against the CSS custom properties in both themes and found no mismatch
events.scope: color token values and their documented roles; measured with a script and confirmed by rendering both themes in headless Chromium, not by eyeballing

events.summary: Three independent review lanes ran on the diff before the PR: Go correctness passed with one real gap (the invalid-end 400 branch was never reached by a test); XSS review passed, correcting the orchestrator's wrong premise that no escaping helper existed (esc() predates the diff and every CR-derived string goes through it) and leaving one defense-in-depth note on four int32 counters whose CRD schema already types them as integers; UI review found the new expandable rows lacked the keyboard and aria-expanded treatment the same diff gave sortable headers, and that the error banner had no alert role
events.scope: review coverage of server.go, server_test.go and dashboard.html between f9e328e and afb7150; reviewers were read-only and separate from the authoring lanes

events.summary: Review follow-ups (d5b403d): expandable rows in the quotas, orphans and quota-policies tables get tabindex and aria-expanded and are toggled by the existing delegated Enter/Space handler, with no role=button on the tr so row and cell semantics survive; the error banner is role=alert; the four counters go through esc(); TestHandleAPIHistory_InvalidRange gains a valid-start/unparseable-end case

The new invalid-end test case passes and exercises the previously unreached branch; Enter and Space on a focused policy row flip aria-expanded true/false with the default action prevented and focus retained, and the error banner reports role=alert -- observed in headless Chromium serving this tree's dashboard.html with /api proxied to the live agent
events.scope: keyboard operability and ARIA state of expandable rows, alert role, and the invalid-end 400 branch; the working tree served, not a rebuilt image

events.summary: make test passed with no FAIL across all packages, go vet ./... and gofmt -l . were clean, and golangci-lint v2.12.2 (the CI-pinned version) reported 0 issues. Against the live cluster: /api/history returned 400 for a malformed timestamp, a lone bound and start >= end, 200 with the range echoed for a valid custom range, and period-only calls unchanged; a real path split into 5 and 7 entries across two adjacent 30-minute windows summing to the full set. The deployed image's dashboard.html was byte-identical to the tree before the follow-up commit, and the trends custom range, empty state, Quota Policies tab, detail row and dark theme were rendered in headless Chromium
events.scope: unit, static and lint checks repository-wide; API contract and rendering against a live cluster for internal/ui only. Nothing here exercises quota enforcement -- internal/quota is untouched and no prjquota-host claim is made

events.summary: The two OpenForge gaps are closed and the four dashboard changes are landed, reviewed by three separate lanes and re-verified, within the scope stated in e2 and at the evidence level stated in e10
Complete for internal/ui at the unit, lint, live-API and rendered-UI level; #96 tracks the pre-existing path-less /api/history behaviour that was deliberately left out
